lines.label: with the caption
lines.prompt: H&E, FFPE, rectum, adenocarcinoma, nos. 0.75 µm per pixel.
lines.note: The tissue image displays well-differentiated, orderly spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells typical of the rectum's muscularis propria. Nuclei are elongated, centrally located, within eosinophilic cytoplasm. Minor inflammatory infiltration is present. No signs of dysplasia or malignancy are evident. Variability in cell density suggests mild injury or normal variation. Overall, the tissue appears healthy.

lines.label: with the caption
lines.prompt: H&E, FFPE, liver and intrahepatic bile ducts, hepatocellular carcinoma, nos. 0.75 µm per pixel.
lines.note: The liver tissue shows dense cellular infiltration with medium to large cells, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei, and prominent nucleoli, indicative of high proliferation. Disrupted hepatic architecture, irregular cells, mitotic figures, necrosis, and hepatocyte loss suggest a malignant neoplasm, likely hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma.

lines.prompt: H&E, FFPE, bronchus and lung, squamous cell carcinoma, nos. 0.75 µm per pixel.
lines.note: The microscopic image displays a heterogeneous cell population with pleomorphism, large hyperchromatic and irregular-shaped nuclei (nuclear atypia), high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratios, and eosinophilic or vacuolated cytoplasm. Features like mucin, disorganized tissue architecture, and scattered inflammatory cells suggest a diagnosis of mucinous adenocarcinoma of the lung.
